title: API credential is hard-coded in client JavaScript and sent as a Bearer token from the browser
evidence: api.js:3 defines the key; api.js:6 and api.js:11 send it as Authorization. index.html:25 serves api.js to every visitor. Driven: the page loaded api.js and issued requests with it.
failing_case: Anyone who opens the page (View Source or the Network tab) reads the key and can call the orders and refunds endpoints with it, including POST /refunds.
remediation: Remove the key from the client. Put a server-side proxy in front of the API that holds the key, authenticates the user and enforces who may refund. Rotate the shipped key.

title: Customer name is written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 builds a row string with o.customer.name and assigns it through innerHTML. Driven with a mocked API returning name '' on the visible page: window.__xss became 1.
failing_case: A customer who registers with the name runs script in the staff member's session on OrderDesk, where the key and refund action are available.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent (or escape every interpolated value). Apply the same to data-id and o.status in the same template.

quote: - **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key never leaves the server; it is shipped in the browser script
evidence: api.js:3 holds the key in a public file; api.js:6 and :11 send it from the browser.
failing_case: A reviewer or customer who trusts this line deploys it as is and leaks the key.
remediation: Fix the code first (server-side proxy), then keep the sentence; otherwise delete it.

quote: - Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README says refunds are confirmed before sending; there is no confirmation step
evidence: app.js:49-52 sends on first click; no confirm() or dialog in index.html or app.js. Driven: one click posted to /refunds.
failing_case: A user trusts the line, clicks Refund selected by accident, and the refund is sent immediately.
remediation: Add the confirm step in the code or remove the line.

title: HTTP status is never checked; an error body or a rejected fetch breaks the page with no message
evidence: api.js:6-7 returns res.json() whatever the status. app.js:41 has no try/catch. Driven: API answering 500 with {"error":"x"} gave an uncaught 'orders is not iterable'; stats and table stayed blank with no message.
failing_case: The orders API returns 500 or the user is offline: the dashboard shows an empty card area and no table, with no cause or retry. After a prior success, the old data stays on screen under the new filter.
remediation: Throw when !res.ok, catch in load(), render an error state with the cause and a Retry control, and validate that the body is an array.

title: refund() never awaits or checks the POST and always returns ok: true
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await or catch; api.js:12 returns ok:true immediately. Driven: with POST /refunds answered 500, the toast still read 'Refunded 2 orders!' (app.js:51). A network failure is an unhandled rejection.
failing_case: The refunds API returns 500 or the device is offline; the staff member sees 'Refunded 2 orders!' and believes money was returned to customers. Double-click sends the request twice because the control is never disabled.
remediation: await the fetch, throw on !res.ok, return the parsed result, and have the caller show success only on a confirmed response and an error with a retry otherwise. Disable the control while in flight and send an idempotency key.

title: Pagination starts at page 1 but the offset is page * PAGE_SIZE, so the first 10 orders are never shown
evidence: app.js:3 sets page = 1; app.js:27 computes start = 10. Driven: with 25 orders, 'Page 1' showed the order with id 11 first.
failing_case: On first load the user sees orders 11-20 labelled Page 1; orders 1-10 are only reachable by pressing Prev to page 0, which is labelled 'Page 0'. The newest orders are hidden on load.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE, or make page zero-based and display page + 1. Cover it with a test.

title: Selection list only grows: unchecking never removes, duplicates are kept, and re-render clears boxes but not the list
evidence: app.js:35 pushes on check and ignores uncheck; renderTable rebuilds the rows unchecked; selected is never emptied after a refund (app.js:49-52). Driven: checked and unchecked row 1, checked row 2, paged next/prev; selected = ['11','12'] with 0 boxes checked, and Refund sent both.
failing_case: The user ticks order 11, unticks it, ticks order 12 and refunds: the request body contains 11 and 12, so an order they deliberately deselected is refunded. A second click on Refund resends the same ids.
remediation: Keep selected as a Set keyed by id: add on check, delete on uncheck, re-apply checked state when rendering, clear it after a confirmed refund.

title: Refund fires on one click with no confirmation, no count check and no undo
evidence: app.js:49-52 calls refund(selected) directly. Driven: with an empty selection the click still POSTs and shows 'Refunded 0 orders!'.
failing_case: A mis-click on Refund selected sends the refund for every ticked id immediately; with nothing ticked it posts an empty list and reports success.
remediation: Disable the button while selection is empty. Show a confirm step that states the count and total before sending.

title: The main action is a span: not focusable, no role, not operable by keyboard
evidence: index.html:19. Driven: tagName SPAN, tabIndex -1. Click handler is bound in app.js:49 only for pointer.
failing_case: A keyboard or screen-reader user tabs through the toolbar and never reaches 'Refund selected'; the page's one primary action cannot be used (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2, level A).
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn"> and keep the styling on the class. Disable it when nothing is selected.

title: Text contrast fails 4.5:1 in several places, at 11-12 px
evidence: #aaa on #fff (.lbl, styles.css:9) is about 2.3:1; the Prev/Next buttons (styles.css:18) are #aaa 12px on #F4F1EA, lower still; the eyebrow (styles.css:4) is #c7c2f0 11px on a #6366f1 to #8b5cf6 gradient; the yellow status dot #cc3 on white is under 3:1 too.
failing_case: A user with low vision cannot read the card labels (REVENUE, ORDERS), the pager buttons or the eyebrow line (WCAG 1.4.3, AA).
remediation: Use colours measured at 4.5:1 or better (for example #595959 on white), and raise small text to at least 12-14 px. Pager controls need a visible boundary.

title: Fixed 1000 px table and 3-column card grid break the layout on a phone
evidence: styles.css:13 and :6; there are no media queries. Driven at 390 px: document scrollWidth was 1024.
failing_case: At 390 px the user must scroll sideways to see the table and the status column, and at 200% zoom the same happens at desktop widths (WCAG 1.4.10).
remediation: Use width: 100% with a wrapper that scrolls or a stacked row layout under 640 px, and change the card grid to one column below 600 px.

title: Focus outlines are removed on buttons, inputs and selects with no replacement
evidence: styles.css:19. Driven: computed outline-style of the focused search box is 'none'. Prev/Next buttons are #aaa with no border, so focus gives no visible change.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabbing through search, status, Prev and Next cannot see where focus is (WCAG 2.4.7, AA).
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1d4ed8; outline-offset: 2px; } on every control.

quote: - **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: README claims WCAG 2.1 AA and 44 px targets; the page fails both
evidence: Focus removed (styles.css:19), contrast ~2.3:1 (styles.css:9), a span as the main button (index.html:19), no labels, no names. The pager buttons are 12px with 2px 4px padding (styles.css:18). 2.5.5 is a AAA criterion in WCAG 2.1, not AA.
failing_case: A buyer relying on 'meets WCAG 2.1 AA' ships the dashboard to staff who use a keyboard or screen reader and cannot refund.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit passes. Cite 2.5.5 as AAA if a 44 px target is a goal.

title: Every keystroke fires an unthrottled fetch, and the last response to arrive wins, not the last request
evidence: app.js:45 binds load to oninput. app.js:41 assigns orders after await with no sequence check or abort.
failing_case: The user types 'ann'; the response for 'an' is slower than the one for 'ann' and lands last, so the table and stats show results for 'an' while the box reads 'ann'. Each keystroke also costs one API call.
remediation: Debounce the input (about 250 ms), abort the previous request with AbortController or ignore any response whose sequence number is stale.

quote: - **Pricing:** the Team plan is $15 per seat; 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong
evidence: 12 x $15 = $180. If $15 is monthly: 180 x 12 = $2,160, less 20% = $1,728 a year. If $15 is yearly: $180, less 20% = $144. $1,440 matches neither.
failing_case: A buyer quoted $1,440 is under-charged by $288 on the monthly reading, or over-quoted tenfold on the yearly reading.
remediation: State the billing period of the $15 and correct the total ($1,728 or $144).

title: Search text is put into the URL unencoded
evidence: api.js:6 interpolates query raw. Driven: typing 'a&status=refunded#' produced the request .../orders?q=a&status=refunded, truncating the query at the # and injecting a status parameter.
failing_case: A customer search for 'Smith & Sons' sends q=Smith and a stray ' Sons' key; names with # or + return the wrong orders.
remediation: Use encodeURIComponent on each value or build the query with URLSearchParams.

title: Empty result shows '$NaN' as AVG ORDER
evidence: app.js:18 divides by orders.length with no guard. Driven: API returning [] rendered '$NaN AVG ORDER'. The average also divides net revenue by all orders, including pending and refunded.
failing_case: A search matching no customers shows '$NaN' in the stats card.
remediation: Return 0 (or an em dash) when there are no orders; define the average over paid orders in the domain function.

title: Prev and Next have no bounds, and the page count uses floor
evidence: app.js:47-48 change page without limits; app.js:34 uses Math.floor(orders.length / PAGE_SIZE). Driven: Prev twice showed 'Page -1 of 2' with an empty table; Next five times showed 'Page 4 of 2' with 0 rows; 25 orders reported 2 pages, and an empty result 'Page 1 of 0'. Filter changes (app.js:41) do not reset page.
failing_case: A user presses Next past the end and sees an empty table with 'Page 4 of 2'. With 25 orders the last 5 are on no counted page. After searching from page 3, the new result list may show zero rows.
remediation: Compute pages with Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page in one setter, disable Prev/Next at the ends, and reset page to 1 in load().

title: '10,000 orders instantly' is unmeasured and the code is built for 10 rows a page
evidence: app.js:41-42 recomputes stats over every order (and fires on each keystroke, app.js:45); app.js:32 uses innerHTML += per row; no benchmark exists in the repo. Not measured.
failing_case: No 10,000-row run is recorded, so the claim cannot be checked; each keystroke refetches the full list and rebuilds all stats.
remediation: Measure with 10,000 rows and quote the time, or delete the claim.

title: Pricing rules (loyalty discount, 8.25% tax, refund sign) live in the render function, in floating point
evidence: app.js:9-17: discount and tax constants are inline in renderStats. The table shows raw o.total (app.js:32) while stats show a taxed and discounted figure, so the same order has two different values on screen.
failing_case: A gold customer's $100 paid order is listed as $100 in the table but contributes $97.43 to Revenue (100*0.9*1.0825). A tax-rate change needs an edit inside DOM code, and 0.1-style float sums drift.
remediation: Move the calculation into one pure, tested function (integer cents or a decimal library) and have the view display its result. Say whether totals already include tax and discount.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured dot with no text or name
evidence: app.js:32 renders an empty span; styles.css:17 sets green, red, yellow.
failing_case: A colour-blind user cannot tell paid from refunded (red/green), and a screen-reader user hears nothing in the Status column (WCAG 1.4.1, level A).
remediation: Print the status word beside the dot (or give the dot an accessible name) and use shapes or text, not hue alone.

title: Search box, status select and row checkboxes have no accessible name
evidence: index.html:17-18 have no label; the placeholder is the only text. The first th (index.html:21) is empty, and the row checkboxes (app.js:32) have no label.
failing_case: A screen-reader user hears 'edit text' and 'combo box', and 'checkbox' for each row without knowing which order it refunds (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2).
remediation: Add visible or aria-labels: 'Search customers', 'Filter by status', and 'Select order <id> for <customer>' on each checkbox; give the first th visually hidden text.

title: The refund result is not announced and never goes away
evidence: index.html:23 has no role="status" or aria-live; app.js:51 sets display:block and nothing hides it. styles.css:20 pulses it forever.
failing_case: A screen-reader user presses Refund and hears nothing; a sighted user sees the toast stay for the rest of the session, including after later errors.
remediation: Give the toast role="status" (role="alert" for errors), keep it in the DOM, and hide it after a few seconds or on dismiss.

title: Toast pulses forever and ignores prefers-reduced-motion
evidence: styles.css:20-21 define an infinite scale animation; no @media (prefers-reduced-motion) exists in the file.
failing_case: A user with vestibular sensitivity who set reduced motion still sees a constantly scaling box once a refund is sent (WCAG 2.2.2 for anything over 5 s, level A).
remediation: Remove the infinite animation (a single short fade is enough) and wrap any motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

title: Success toast with an exclamation mark and wrong grammar for one order, claimed before any confirmation
evidence: app.js:51. Singular case yields 'Refunded 1 orders!'.
failing_case: Refunding one order reads 'Refunded 1 orders!'.
remediation: Pluralise correctly, drop the exclamation mark, and word the message only after the server confirms.

quote: td:nth-child(2) { max-width: 120px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }
title: Customer names are clipped at 120 px with no ellipsis or full-text access
evidence: styles.css:15 hides overflow without text-overflow; max-width on a table cell is ignored unless the table layout allows it.
failing_case: Two customers named 'Alexandra Montgomery-Smith' and 'Alexandra Montgomery-Jones' can show identically as 'Alexandra Montgomery-'.
remediation: Add text-overflow: ellipsis and a title or wrap the text.
